title: Mi vida
goal: Talk about your life across past, present and future, give opinions and link your ideas.

lessons.title: In my opinion
lessons.notes:
To give an opinion:
**creo que** · **pienso que** (I think that) · **me parece que** (it seems to me) · **en mi opinión** · **para mí** (for me)
**Creo que es una buena idea.** = I think it's a good idea.
To agree or disagree: **estoy de acuerdo** (I agree) · **no estoy de acuerdo** · **tienes razón** (you're right).
Ask for someone's view: **¿Qué piensas?** · **¿Qué te parece?** (What do you think of it?)
One tip for later: **no creo que** is followed by a different verb form (the subjunctive, at B1). For now, say **creo que no** = I don't think so.

lessons.title: Linking ideas
lessons.notes:
Linking words turn short sentences into real speech:
**además** (also, besides) · **aunque** (although) · **sin embargo** (however) · **así que** (so) · **porque** (because) · **o sea** (I mean)
**Me gusta mi trabajo, aunque es difícil.**
**Estaba cansado; sin embargo, fui a la fiesta.**
**Llovía, así que nos quedamos en casa.**
**porque** answers "why" in the middle of a sentence; to start with the reason, use **como**: **Como llovía, nos quedamos en casa.**
Don't confuse **por qué** (why? - two words, accent) with **porque** (because).

lessons.title: My story
lessons.notes:
Telling your life story brings all the tenses together:
**Preterite** for events: **Nací en Brisbane.** (I was born) **Me mudé a Sídney en 2015.** (I moved)
**Imperfect** for background: **De niño vivía cerca del mar.**
**Present perfect** for experience up to now: **He vivido en tres países.**
**Present** for now: **Ahora trabajo en un hospital.**
**hace** + time + **que** + present = how long something has been going on: **Hace cinco años que vivo aquí.** = I've lived here for five years.
**desde** works too: **Vivo aquí desde 2020.**
**nacer** (to be born) is regular in the preterite: **nací, naciste, nació**.

lessons.title: Hopes and plans
lessons.notes:
To talk about the future in a softer way:
**me gustaría** + infinitive = I would like to: **Me gustaría vivir en Chile.**
**espero** + infinitive = I hope to: **Espero viajar el año que viene.**
**tener ganas de** + infinitive = to feel like / look forward to: **Tengo ganas de verte.**
**pienso** + infinitive = I'm planning to: **Pienso estudiar más.**
And of course **voy a** + infinitive and the future: **Algún día hablaré español muy bien.**
**el sueño** is both a dream and sleepiness: **tengo sueño** = I'm sleepy.
